In mathematics, '''orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle''' are families of [[Orthogonal polynomials|polynomials that are orthogonal with respect to integration]] over the [[unit circle]] in the [[complex plane]], for some [[probability measure]] on the unit circle. They were  introduced  by {{harvs|txt|last=Szegő|year1=1920|year2=1921|year3=1939}}.

==Definition==

Let <math>\mu</math> be a probability measure on the unit circle <math>\mathbb{T} =\{z\in\mathbb{C} :|z|=1\}</math> and assume <math>\mu</math> is nontrivial, i.e., its [[support (mathematics)|support]] is an [[infinite set]]. By a combination of the [[Radon–Nikodym theorem|Radon-Nikodym]]
and [[Lebesgue's decomposition theorem|Lebesgue decomposition]] theorems, any such measure can be uniquely
decomposed into
:<math>d\mu =w(\theta) \frac{d\theta}{2\pi} + d\mu_s</math>,
where <math>d\mu_s</math> is '' singular''  with respect to <math>d\theta/2\pi</math> and <math>w \in L^{1}(\mathbb{T})</math> with <math>wd\theta/2\pi</math> the ''absolutely continuous part'' of <math>d\mu</math>.{{sfn|Simon|2005a|page=43}}

The orthogonal polynomials associated with <math>\mu</math> are defined as
:<math>\Phi_n(z)=z^n + \text{lower order}</math>,
such that
:<math>\int \bar{z}^j\Phi_n(z)\,d\mu(z) =0, \quad j = 0,1,\dots,n-1</math>.

==The Szegő recurrence ==

The monic orthogonal Szegő polynomials satisfy a recurrence relation of the form 
:<math>\Phi_{n+1}(z)=z\Phi_n(z)-\overline\alpha_n\Phi_n^*(z)</math>
:<math>\Phi_{n+1}^{\ast}(z)=\Phi_n^{\ast}(z)-\alpha_n z\Phi_n(z)</math>
for <math>n \geq 0</math> and initial condition <math>\Phi_0=1</math>, with
:<math>\Phi_n^*(z)=z^n\overline{\Phi_n(1/\overline{z})}</math>
and constants <math>\alpha_n</math> in the open unit disk <math> \mathbb{D} = \{ z\in \mathbb{C} : |z|<1\} </math> given by
:<math>\alpha_n = -\overline{\Phi_{n+1}(0)}</math>

called the '''Verblunsky coefficients'''. {{sfn|Simon|2010|page=44}} Moreover,
:<math>\|\Phi_{n+1}\|^{2} = \prod_{j=0}^{n} (1-|\alpha_j|^2) = (1-|\alpha_n|^2)\|\Phi_n\|^2 </math>.
Geronimus' theorem states that the Verblunsky coefficients associated with <math>d\mu</math> are the [[Schur class|Schur parameters]]:{{sfn|Simon|2010|page=74}}
:<math> \alpha_n(d\mu) = \gamma_n</math>

===Verblunsky's theorem===

[[Samuel Verblunsky|Verblunsky]]'s theorem states that for any sequence of numbers <math>\{\alpha_{j}^{(0)}\}_{j=0}^{\infty}</math> in <math> \mathbb{D} </math> there is a unique nontrivial probability measure <math>\mu </math> on <math>\mathbb{T}</math> with <math>\alpha_j(d\mu)=\alpha_j^{(0)}</math>.{{sfn|Schmüdgen|2017|page=265}}

===Baxter's theorem===

Baxter's theorem states that the Verblunsky coefficients form an absolutely convergent series [[if and only if]] the moments of <math>\mu</math> form an absolutely convergent series and the weight function <math>w</math> is strictly positive everywhere.{{sfn|Simon|2005a|page=313}}

==Szegő's theorem==
For any nontrivial probability measure <math>d\mu</math> on <math>\mathbb{T}</math>, Verblunsky's form of [[Szegő limit theorems|Szegő's theorem]] states that 
:<math>\prod_{n = 0}^\infty(1-|\alpha_n|^2) = \exp\big(\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log w(\theta)\,d\theta\big).</math>
The left-hand side is independent of <math>d\mu_s</math> but unlike Szegő's original version, where <math>d\mu = d\mu_{ac}</math>, Verblunsky's form does allow <math>d\mu_s \neq 0 </math>.{{sfn|Simon|2010|page=29}} Subsequently,
:<math>\sum_{n = 0}^\infty |\alpha_n|^2 < \infty \;\iff\; \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log w(\theta)\,d\theta > -\infty</math>.
One of the consequences is the existence of a mixed spectrum for discretized Schrödinger operators.{{sfn | Totik | 2016 | page=269}}

==Rakhmanov's theorem==

Rakhmanov's theorem states that if the absolutely continuous part <math>w</math> of the measure <math>\mu</math> is positive [[almost everywhere]] then the Verblunsky coefficients <math>\alpha_n</math> tend to 0.

==Examples==

The [[Rogers–Szegő polynomials]] are an example of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.
